3: The Right Tool of the Job

Experimental Elixir.title: Experimental Elixir
Experimental Elixir.desc_long: Beginning at 3rd level, whenever you finish a long rest, you can magically produce an experimental elixir in an empty flask you touch. Roll on the Experimental Elixir table for the elixir's effect, which is triggered when someone drinks the elixir. As an action, a creature can drink the elixir or administer it to an incapacitated creature. You can create additional experimental elixirs by expending a spell slot of 1st lvl or higher for each one. When you do so, you use your action to create the elixir in an empty flask you touch, and you choose the elixir's effect from the Experimental Elixir table. Creating an experimental elixir requires you to have alchemist supplies on your person, and any elixir you create with this feature lasts until it is drunk or until the end of your next long rest. When you reach certain levels in this class, you can make more elixirs at the end of a long rest: 2 at 6th lvl and 3 at 15th lvl. Roll for each elixir's effect separately. Each elixir requires its own flask.
Experimental Elixir.desc_short: Beginning at 3rd level, whenever you finish a long rest, you can magically produce an experimental elixir in an empty flask you touch. Roll on the Experimental Elixir table for the elixir's effect, which is triggered when someone drinks the elixir. As an action, a creature can drink the elixir or administer it to an incapacitated creature.

Alchemical Savant.title: Alchemical Savant
Alchemical Savant.desc_long: At 5th level, you've developed masterful command of magical chemicals, enhancing the healing and damage you create through them. Whenever you cast a spell using your alchemist's supplies as the spellcasting focus, you gain a bonus to one roll of the spell. That roll must restore hit points or be a damage roll that deals acid, fire, necrotic, or poison damage, and the bonus equals your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

Restorative Reagents.title: Restorative Reagents
Restorative Reagents.desc_long:
Starting at 9th level, you can incorporate restorative reagents into some of your works:
- Whenever a creature drinks an experimental elixir you created, the creature gains temporary hit points equal to 2d6 + your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 temporary hit point).
- You can cast Lesser Restoration without expending a spell slot and without preparing the spell, provided you use alchemist's supplies as the spellcasting focus. You can do so a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Chemical Mastery.title: Chemical Mastery
Chemical Mastery.desc_long:
By 15th level, you have been exposed to so many chemicals that they pose little risk to you, and you can use them to quickly end certain ailments:
- You gain resistance to acid damage and poison damage, and you are now immune to the poisoned condition.
- You can cast Greater Restoration and Heal without expending a spell slot, without preparing the spell, and without providing the material component, provided you use alchemist’s supplies as the spellcasting focus. Once you cast either spell with this feature, you can't cast that spell with it again until you finish a long rest.

Arcane Armor.title: Arcane Armor
Arcane Armor.desc_long: Beginning at 3rd level, your metallurgical pursuits have led to you making armor a conduit for your magic. As an action, you can turn a suit of armor you are wearing into Arcane Armor, provided you have smith's tools in hand. You gain the following benefits while wearing this armor: If the armor normally has a Strength requirement, the arcane armor lacks this requirement for you. You can use the arcane armor as a spellcasting focus for your artificer spells. The armor attaches to you and can’t be removed against your will. It also expands to cover your entire body, although you can retract or deploy the helmet as a bonus action. The armor replaces any missing limbs, functioning identically to a body part it is replacing. You can doff or don the armor as an action. The armor continues to be Arcane Armor until you don another suit of armor or you die.
Arcane Armor.desc_short: As an action, you can turn a suit of armor you are wearing into Arcane Armor, provided you have smith's tools in hand. You gain the following benefits while wearing this armor: If the armor normally has a Strength requirement, the arcane armor lacks this requirement for you. You can use the armor as a spellcasting focus. The armor attaches to you and can’t be removed against your will. The armor replaces any missing limbs, functioning identically to a body part it is replacing. You can don or duff the armor as an action.

Armor Model.title: Armor Model
Armor Model.desc_long: At 5th level, you've developed masterful command of magical chemicals, enhancing the healing and damage you create through them. Whenever you cast a spell using your alchemist's supplies as the spellcasting focus, you gain a bonus to one roll of the spell. That roll must restore hit points or be a damage roll that deals acid, fire, necrotic, or poison damage, and the bonus equals your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).
Armor Model.desc_short: Beginning at 3rd level, you can customize your Arcane Armor. When you do so, choose one of the following armor models: Guardian or Infiltrator. The model you choose gives you special benefits while you wear it. Each model includes a special weapon. When you attack with that weapon, you can add your Intelligence modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, to the attack and damage rolls. You can change the armor's model whenever you finish a short or long rest, provided you have smith's tools in hand.

Armor Model: Guardian.title: Armor Model: Guardian
Armor Model: Guardian.desc_long:
Guardian. You design your armor to be in the front line of conflict. It has the following features:
- Thunder Gauntlets. Each of the armor's gauntlets counts as a simple melee weapon while you aren't holding anything in it, and it deals 1d8 thunder damage on a hit. A creature hit by the gauntlet has disadvantage on attack rolls against targets other than you until the start of your next turn, as the armor magically emits a distracting pulse when the creature attacks someone else.
- Defensive Field. As a bonus action, you can gain temporary hit points equal to your level in this class, replacing any temporary hit points you already have. You lose these temporary hit points if you doff the armor. You can use this bonus action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Armor Model: Infiltrator.title: Armor Model: Infiltrator
Armor Model: Infiltrator.desc_long:
Infiltrator. You customize your armor for subtle undertakings. It has the following features:
- Lightning Launcher. A gemlike node appears on one of your armored fists or on the chest (your choice). It counts as a simple ranged weapon, with a normal range of 90 feet and a long range of 300 feet, and it deals 1d6 lightning damage on a hit. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with it, you can deal an extra 1d6 lightning damage to that target.
- Powered Steps. Your walking speed increases by 5 feet.
- Dampening Field. You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. If the armor normally imposes disadvantage on such checks, the advantage and disadvantage cancel each other, as normal.

Extra Attack.title: Extra Attack
Extra Attack.desc_long: Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Armor Modifications.title: Armor Modifications
Armor Modifications.desc_long: At 9th level, you learn how to use your artificer infusions to specially modify your Arcane Armor. That armor now counts as separate items for the purposes of your Infuse Items feature: armor (the chest piece), boots, helmet, and the armor's special weapon. Each of those items can bear one of your infusions, and the infusions transfer over if you change your armor's model with the Armor Model feature. In addition, the maximum number of items you can infuse at once increases by 2, but those extra items must be part of your Arcane Armor.

Perfected Armor.title: Perfected Armor
Perfected Armor.desc_long:
At 15th level, your Arcane Armor gains additional benefits based on its model, as shown below.
Guardian. When a Huge or smaller creature you can see ends its turn within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to magically force it to make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you pull the creature up to 25 feet directly to an unoccupied space. If you pull the target to a space within 5 feet of you, you can make a melee weapon attack against it as part of this reaction. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.
Infiltrator. Any creature that takes lightning damage from your Lightning Launcher glimmers with magical light until the start of your next turn. The glimmering creature sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius, and it has disadvantage on attack rolls against you, as the light jolts it if it attacks you. In addition, the next attack roll against it has advantage, and if that attack hits, the target takes an extra 1d6 lightning damage.
Perfected Armor.desc_short: At 15th level, your Arcane Armor gains additional benefits based on its model.

Eldritch Cannon.title: Eldritch Cannon
Eldritch Cannon.desc_long: You've learned how to create a magical cannon. Using woodcarver's tools or smith's tools, you can take an action to magically create a Small or Tiny eldritch cannon in an unoccupied space on a horizontal surface within 5 feet of you. A Small eldritch cannon occupies its space, and a Tiny one can be held in one hand. Once you create a cannon, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest or until you expend a spell slot to create one. You can have only one cannon at a time and can't create one while your cannon is present. The cannon is a magical object. Regardless of size, the cannon has an AC of 18 and a number of hit points equal to five times your artificer level. It is immune to poison damage and psychic damage. If it is forced to make an ability check or a saving throw, treat all its ability scores as 10 (+0). If the mending spell is cast on it, it regains 2d6 hit points. It disappears if it is reduced to 0 hit points or after 1 hour. You can dismiss it early as an action. When you create the cannon, you determine its appearance and whether it has legs. You also decide which type it is, choosing from the options on the Eldritch Cannons table. On each of your turns, you can take a bonus action to cause the cannon to activate if you are within 60 feet of it. As part of the same bonus action, you can direct the cannon to walk or climb up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space, provided it has legs.
Eldritch Cannon.desc_short: You've learned how to create a magical cannon. Using woodcarver's tools or smith's tools, you can take an action to magically create a Small or Tiny eldritch cannon in an unoccupied space on a horizontal surface within 5 feet of you. A Small eldritch cannon occupies its space, and a Tiny one can be held in one hand. Once you create a cannon, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest or until you expend a spell slot to create one. You can have only one cannon at a time and can't create one while your cannon is present.

Arcane Firearm.title: Arcane Firearm
Arcane Firearm.desc_long: At 5th level, You know how to turn a wand, staff, or rod into an arcane firearm, a conduit for your destructive spells. When you finish a long rest, you can use woodcarver's tools to carve special sigils into a wand, staff, or rod and thereby turn it into your arcane firearm. The sigils disappear from the object if you later carve them on a different item. The sigils otherwise last indefinitely. You can use your arcane firearm as a spellcasting focus for your artificer spells. When you cast an artificer spell through the firearm, roll a d8, and you gain a bonus to one of the spell's damage rolls equal to the number rolled.

Explosive Cannon.title: Explosive Cannon
Explosive Cannon.desc_long:
Starting at 9th level, every eldritch cannon you create is more destructive:
- The cannon's damage rolls all increase by 1d8.
- As an action, you can command the cannon to detonate if you are within 60 feet of it. Doing so destroys the cannon and forces each creature within 20 feet of it to make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking 3d8 force damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Fortified Position.title: Fortified Position
Fortified Position.desc_long:
By 15th level, you’re a master at forming well-defended emplacements using Eldritch Cannon:
- You and your allies have half cover while within 10 feet of a cannon you create with Eldritch Cannon, as a result of a shimmering field of magical protection that the cannon emits.
- You can now have two cannons at the same time. You can create two with the same action (but not the same spell slot), and you can activate both of them with the same bonus action. You determine whether the cannons are identical to each other or different. You can't create a third cannon while you have two.

Battle Ready.title: Battle Ready
Battle Ready.desc_long:
When you reach 3rd level, your combat training and your experiments with magic have paid off in two ways:
- You gain proficiency with martial weapons.
- When you attack with a magic weapon, you can use your Intelligence modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity modifier, for the attack and damage rolls.

Steel Defender.title: Steel Defender
Steel Defender.desc_long: By 3rd level, your tinkering has borne you a faithful companion, a steel defender. It's friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your commands. See its game statistics in the Steel Defender stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places. You determine the creature's appearance and whether it has two legs or four; your choice has no effect on its game statistics. In combat, the defender shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but the only action it takes on its turn is the Dodge action, unless you take a bonus action on your turn to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or some other action. If you are incapacitated, the defender can take any action of its choice, not just Dodge. If the Mending spell is cast on it, it regains 2d6 hit points. If it has died within the last hour, you can use your smith's tools as an action to revive it, provided you are within 5 feet of it and you expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher. The steel defender returns to life after 1 minute with all its hit points restored. At the end of a long rest, you can create a new steel defender if you have smith's tools with you. If you already have a defender from this feature, the first one immediately perishes. The defender also perishes if you die.
Steel Defender.desc_short: By 3rd level, your tinkering has borne you a faithful companion, a steel defender. It's friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your commands. See its game statistics in the Steel Defender stat block, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places. You determine the creature's appearance and whether it has two legs or four; your choice has no effect on its game statistics.

Extra Attack.title: Extra Attack
Extra Attack.desc_long: Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Arcane Jolt.title: Arcane Jolt
Arcane Jolt.desc_long:
At 9th level, you've learned new ways to channel arcane energy to harm or heal. When either you hit a target with a magic weapon attack or your steel defender hits a target, you can channel magical energy through the strike to create one of the following effects:
The target takes an extra 2d6 force damage.
Choose one creature or object you can see within 30 feet of the target. Healing energy flows into the chosen recipient, restoring 2d6 hit points to it.
You can use this energy a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), but you can do so no more than once on a turn. You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Improved Defender.title: Improved Defender
Improved Defender.desc_long:
At 15th level, your Arcane Jolt and steel defender become more powerful:
- The extra damage and the healing of your Arcane Jolt both increase to 4d6.
- Your steel defender gains a +2 bonus to Armor Class.
- Whenever your steel defender uses its Deflect Attack, the attacker takes force damage equal to 1d4 + your Intelligence modifier.

Ancestral Protectors.title: Ancestral Protectors
Ancestral Protectors.desc_long: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, spectral warriors appear when you enter your rage. While you're raging, the first creature you hit with an attack on your turn becomes the target of the warriors, which hinder its attacks. Until the start of your next turn, that target has disadvantage on any attack roll that isn't against you, and when the target hits a creature other than you with an attack, that creature has resistance to the damage dealt by the attack. The effect on the target ends early if your rage ends.

Spirit Shield.title: Spirit Shield
Spirit Shield.desc_long: Beginning at 6th level, the guardian spirits that aid you can provide supernatural protection to those you defend. If you are raging and another creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to reduce that damage by 2d6. When you reach certain levels in this class, you can reduce the damage by more: by 3d6 at 10th level and by 4d6 at 14th level.

Consult the Spirits.title: Consult the Spirits
Consult the Spirits.desc_long: At 10th level, you gain the ability to consult with your ancestral spirits. When you do so, you cast the Augury or Clairvoyance spell, without using a spell slot or material components. Rather than creating a spherical sensor, this use of clairvoyance invisibly summons one of your ancestral spirits to the chosen location. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells. After you cast either spell in this way, you can't use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

Vengeful Ancestors.title: Vengeful Ancestors
Vengeful Ancestors.desc_long: At 14th level, your ancestral spirits grow powerful enough to retaliate. When you use your Spirit Shield to reduce the damage of an attack, the attacker takes an amount of force damage that your Spirit Shield prevents.

Battlerager Armor.title: Battlerager Armor
Battlerager Armor.desc_long: When you choose this path at 3rd level, you gain the ability to use spiked armor as a weapon. While you are wearing spiked armor and are raging, you can use a bonus action to make one melee weapon attack with your armor spikes against a target within 5 feet of you. If the attack hits, the spikes deal 1d4 piercing damage. You use your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls. Additionally, when you use the Attack action to grapple a creature, the target takes 3 piercing damage if your grapple check succeeds.

Reckless Abandon.title: Reckless Abandon
Reckless Abandon.desc_long: Beginning at 6th level, when you use Reckless Attack while raging, you also gain temporary hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1). They vanish if any of them are left when your rage ends.

Battlerager Charge.title: Battlerager Charge
Battlerager Charge.desc_long: Beginning at 10th level, you can take the Dash action as a bonus action while you are raging.

Spiked Retribution.title: Spiked Retribution
Spiked Retribution.desc_long: Starting at 14th level, when a creature within 5 feet of you hits you with a melee attack, the attacker takes 3 piercing damage if you are raging, aren't incapacitated, and are wearing spiked armor.

Form of the Beast.title: Form of the Beast
Form of the Beast.desc_long:
When you enter your rage, you can transform. Until the rage ends, you manifest a natural weapon. It counts as a simple melee weapon for you, and you add your Strength modifier to the attack and damage rolls when you attack with it, as normal.
Bite. Your mouth transforms into a bestial muzzle or great mandibles (your choice). It deals 1d8 piercing damage on a hit. Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with this bite, you regain a number of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus, provided you have less than half your hit points when you hit.
Claws. Each of your hands transforms into a claw, which you can use as a weapon if it’s empty. It deals 1d6 slashing damage on a hit. Once on each of your turns when you attack with a claw using the Attack action, you can make one additional claw attack as part of the same action.
Tail. You grow a lashing, spiny tail, which deals 1d8 piercing damage on a hit and has the reach property. If a creature you can see within 10 feet of you hits you with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to swipe your tail and roll a d8, applying a bonus to your AC equal to the number rolled, potentially causing the attack to miss you.
Form of the Beast.desc_short: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, when you enter your rage, you can transform, revealing the bestial power within you. Until the rage ends, you manifest a natural weapon. It counts as a simple melee weapon for you, and you add your Strength modifier to the attack and damage rolls when you attack with it, as normal.

Bestial Soul.title: Bestial Soul
Bestial Soul.desc_long:
Beginning at 6th level, the feral power within you increases, causing the natural weapons of your Form of the Beast to count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. You can also alter your form to help you adapt to your surroundings. When you finish a short or long rest, choose one of the following benefits, which lasts until you finish a short or long rest:
- You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed, and you can breathe underwater.
- You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed, and you can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.
- When you jump, you can make a Strength (Athletics) check and extend your jump by a number of feet equal to the check’s total. You can make this special check only once per turn.
Bestial Soul.desc_short: Beginning at 6th level, the feral power within you increases, causing the natural weapons of your Form of the Beast to count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. You can also alter your form to help you adapt to your surroundings.

Infectious Fury.title: Infectious Fury
Infectious Fury.desc_long:
When you hit a creature with your natural weapons while you are raging, the beast within you can curse your target with rabid fury. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your CON modifier + your proficiency bonus) or suffer one of the following effects (your choice):
- The target must use its reaction to make a melee attack against another creature of your choice that you can see.
- Target takes 2d12 psychic damage.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Call the Hunt.title: Call the Hunt
Call the Hunt.desc_long: The beast within you grows so powerful that you can spread its ferocity to others and gain resilience from them joining your hunt. When you enter your rage, you can choose a number of other willing creatures you can see within 30 feet of you equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of one creature). You gain 5 temporary hit points for each creature that accepts this feature. Until the rage ends, the chosen creatures can use the following benefit once on each of their turns: when the creature hits a target with an attack roll and deals damage to it, the creature can roll a d6 and gain a bonus to the damage equal to the number rolled. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

Frenzy.title: Frenzy
Frenzy.desc_long: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you rage. If you do so, for the duration of your rage you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your rage ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion.

Mindless Rage.title: Mindless Rage
Mindless Rage.desc_long: Beginning at 6th level, you can't be charmed or frightened while raging. If you are charmed or frightened when you enter your rage, the effect is suspended for the duration of the rage.

Intimidating Presence.title: Intimidating Presence
Intimidating Presence.desc_long: Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do so, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you. If the creature succeeds on its saving throw, you can't use this feature on that creature again for 24 hours.

Retaliation.title: Retaliation
Retaliation.desc_long: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

Giant's Power.title: Giant's Power
Giant's Power.desc_long: When you choose this path, you learn to speak, read, and write Giant or one other language of your choice if you already know Giant. Additionally, you learn a cantrip of your choice: either druidcraft or thaumaturgy. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell.

Giant's Havoc.title: Giant's Havoc
Giant's Havoc.desc_long:
Your rages pull strength from the primal might of giants, transforming you into a hulking force of destruction. While raging, you gain the following benefits:
- Crushing Throw. When you make a successful ranged attack with a thrown weapon using Strength, you can add your Rage Damage bonus to the attack’s damage roll.
- Giant Stature. Your reach increases by 5 feet, and if you are smaller than Large, you become Large, along with anything you are wearing. If there isn’t enough room for you to increase your size, your size doesn’t change.

Elemental Cleaver.title: Elemental Cleaver
Elemental Cleaver.desc_long: Your bond with the elemental might of giants grows, and you learn to infuse weapons with primordial energy. When you enter your rage, you can choose one weapon that you are holding and infuse it with one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, thunder, or lightning. While you wield the infused weapon during your rage, the weapon’s damage type changes to the chosen type, it deals an extra 1d6 damage of the chosen type when it hits, and it gains the thrown property, with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet. If you throw the weapon, it reappears in your hand the instant after it hits or misses a target. The infused weapon’s benefits are suppressed while a creature other than you wields it. While raging and holding the infused weapon, you can use a bonus action to change the infused weapon’s current damage type to another one from the damage type options above.
Elemental Cleaver.desc_short: Your bond with the elemental might of giants grows, and you learn to infuse weapons with primordial energy. When you enter your rage, you can choose one weapon that you are holding and infuse it with one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, thunder, or lightning.

Mighty Impel.title: Mighty Impel
Mighty Impel.desc_long: Your connection to giant strength allows you to hurl both allies and enemies on the battlefield. As a bonus action while raging, you can choose one Medium or smaller creature within your reach and move it to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself. An unwilling creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) to avoid the effect. If, at the end of this movement, the thrown creature isn’t on a surface or liquid that can support it, the creature falls, taking damage as normal and landing prone.

Demiurgic Colossus.title: Demiurgic Colossus
Demiurgic Colossus.desc_long: The primordial power of your rage intensifies. When you rage, your reach increases by 10 feet, your size can increase to Large or Huge (your choice), and you can use your Mighty Impel to move creatures that are Large or smaller. In addition, the extra damage dealt by your Elemental Cleaver feature increases to 2d6.

Mote of Potential.title: Mote of Potential
Mote of Potential.duration: Until the Bardic Inspiration die is lost
Mote of Potential.desc_long:
Whenever you give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die, you can create a Tiny, intangible, invulnerable mote that orbits within 5 feet of it. When the creature spends the die, the mote adds an effect.
Ability check: the creature rolls the die a second time and keeps whichever roll it prefers.
Attack roll: the mote shatters, and the target plus any creatures of your choice within 5 feet of it must make a Constitution save against your spell save DC or take thunder damage equal to the die result.
Saving throw: the creature gains temporary hit points equal to the die result + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1).
Mote of Potential.desc_short: Whenever you give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die, you can create a Tiny, intangible, invulnerable mote that orbits within 5 feet of it. When the creature spends the die, the mote adds an effect.

Performance of Creation.title: Performance of Creation
Performance of Creation.desc_long: You create one nonmagical item in an open space within 10 feet. It must be Medium or smaller and worth no more than 20 x your bard level in gp, and it lasts a number of hours equal to your proficiency bonus. Only one such item can exist at a time. You can use this again before a long rest by expending a spell slot of 2nd level or higher. The maximum size becomes Large at 6th level and Huge at 14th level.

Animating Performance.title: Animating Performance
Animating Performance.desc_long: You animate a Large or smaller nonmagical item that is not worn or carried, using the Dancing Item stat block (AC 16, HP 10 + 5 x your bard level, speed 30 ft. and fly 30 ft., Force-Empowered Slam for 1d10 + PB force damage). It is friendly, acts on your initiative, and takes the Dodge action unless you use a bonus action to command it. You can command it as part of the same bonus action you use for Bardic Inspiration. It lasts 1 hour, until reduced to 0 HP, or until you die. You can use this again before a long rest by expending a spell slot of 3rd level or higher. Only one dancing item at a time.

Creative Crescendo.title: Creative Crescendo
Creative Crescendo.desc_long: When you use Performance of Creation, you can make several items at once, a number equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum two). Only one can be the maximum size; the rest must be Small or Tiny. If you exceed the limit, you choose which earlier item disappears. The gp value limit no longer applies.

Silver Tongue.title: Silver Tongue
Silver Tongue.desc_long: When you make a Charisma (Persuasion) or Charisma (Deception) check, you can treat any d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

Unsettling Words.title: Unsettling Words
Unsettling Words.duration: Until the start of your next turn
Unsettling Words.desc_long: Spend one use of Bardic Inspiration and choose a creature you can see within 60 feet. Roll the die; the creature subtracts the result from the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

Unfailing Inspiration.title: Unfailing Inspiration
Unfailing Inspiration.desc_long: If a creature adds your Bardic Inspiration die to an ability check, attack roll, or saving throw and the roll still fails, the creature keeps the die.

Universal Speech.title: Universal Speech
Universal Speech.desc_long: Choose a number of creatures within 60 feet equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum one). They magically understand you for 1 hour regardless of language. You can use this again before a long rest by expending a spell slot.

Infectious Inspiration.title: Infectious Inspiration
Infectious Inspiration.desc_long: When a creature within 60 feet uses your Bardic Inspiration die and the roll succeeds, you can use your reaction to give a Bardic Inspiration die to a different creature (not you) within 60 feet that can hear you, without spending one of your uses. You can do this a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum once).

Mantle of Inspiration.title: Mantle of Inspiration
Mantle of Inspiration.desc_long: Spend one use of Bardic Inspiration. Choose up to your Charisma modifier (minimum one) creatures that can see you and that you can see within 60 feet. Each gains 5 temporary hit points and can use its reaction to move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. The temporary hit points become 8 at 5th level, 11 at 10th level, and 14 at 15th level.

Enthralling Performance.title: Enthralling Performance
Enthralling Performance.desc_long: After performing for at least 1 minute, choose up to your Charisma modifier (minimum one) humanoids within 60 feet who watched the whole thing. Each must succeed on a Wisdom save against your spell save DC or be charmed: it idolizes you, praises you, and hinders your opponents while avoiding violence unless already inclined to fight for you. The effect ends after 1 hour, if the target takes damage, if you attack it, or if it sees you attack or damage its allies. A target that succeeds doesn't realize you tried.

Mantle of Majesty.title: Mantle of Majesty
Mantle of Majesty.desc_long: You cast Command without a spell slot and take on an appearance of unearthly beauty for 1 minute, or until your concentration ends. For the duration you can cast Command as a bonus action on each of your turns, with no slot. Creatures charmed by you automatically fail their saves against this Command.

Unbreakable Majesty.title: Unbreakable Majesty
Unbreakable Majesty.desc_long: Your appearance permanently becomes lovelier and fiercer. As a bonus action you can assume a majestic presence for 1 minute or until incapacitated. The first time a creature tries to attack you on a turn, it must make a Charisma save against your spell save DC. On a failure it can't attack you that turn and must pick a new target or waste the attack. On a success it can attack, but has disadvantage on saves against your spells on your next turn.

Bonus Proficiencies.title: Bonus Proficiencies
Bonus Proficiencies.desc_long: You gain proficiency with three skills of your choice.

Cutting Words.title: Cutting Words
Cutting Words.desc_long: When a creature you can see within 60 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, or damage roll, you can use your reaction and spend a Bardic Inspiration use to roll the die and subtract the result from that roll. You can do this after the roll is made but before the DM says whether it succeeds or before damage is dealt. The creature is unaffected if it can't hear you or is immune to being charmed.

Additional Magical Secrets.title: Additional Magical Secrets
Additional Magical Secrets.desc_long: You learn two spells of your choice from any class. Each must be a level you can cast or a cantrip. They count as bard spells for you but don't count against your spells known.

Peerless Skill.title: Peerless Skill
Peerless Skill.desc_long: When you make an ability check, you can spend one use of Bardic Inspiration, roll the die, and add the result to your check. You may do this after seeing your d20 roll but before learning whether you succeed.

Guiding Whispers.title: Guiding Whispers
Guiding Whispers.desc_long: You learn the Guidance cantrip, which doesn't count against your cantrips known. When you cast it, its range is 60 feet.

Spiritual Focus.title: Spiritual Focus
Spiritual Focus.desc_long: You can use a candle, crystal ball, skull, spirit board, or tarokka deck as a spellcasting focus for bard spells. From 6th level, when you cast a damaging or healing bard spell using this focus, roll a d6 and add the result to one damage or healing roll of the spell.

Tales from Beyond.title: Tales from Beyond
Tales from Beyond.desc_long: While holding your Spiritual Focus, use a bonus action and spend a Bardic Inspiration use, then roll your Bardic Inspiration die on the Spirit Tales table. You keep that tale in mind until you use it or finish a short or long rest. As an action, choose a creature you can see within 30 feet (can be you) to receive the effect. Only one tale can be held at a time, and rolling again replaces it. Saves use your spell save DC.

Spirit Session.title: Spirit Session
Spirit Session.duration: Until you start a long rest
Spirit Session.desc_long: During a short or long rest, perform an hour-long ritual with your Spiritual Focus and up to your proficiency bonus in willing creatures (including you). At the end you temporarily learn one spell from any class. It must be Divination or Necromancy, of a level you can cast, and no higher than the number of participants. It counts as a bard spell and doesn't count against spells known. You know it until you start a long rest.

Mystical Connection.title: Mystical Connection
Mystical Connection.desc_long: When you roll on the Spirit Tales table, you can roll the die twice and pick which effect to bestow. If both dice show the same number, you may choose any effect on the table.

Bonus Proficiencies.title: Bonus Proficiencies
Bonus Proficiencies.desc_long: You gain proficiency with medium armor and the scimitar. If you're proficient with a simple or martial melee weapon, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for bard spells.

Fighting Style.title: Fighting Style
Fighting Style.desc_long: Choose one: Dueling (+2 damage with a one-handed melee weapon when no other weapons are wielded) or Two-Weapon Fighting (add your ability modifier to the damage of the off-hand attack). You can't take the same style twice.

Blade Flourish.title: Blade Flourish
Blade Flourish.duration: Until end of turn / start of next turn
Blade Flourish.desc_long: Whenever you take the Attack action, your walking speed increases by 10 feet until the end of the turn. When a weapon attack from that action hits, you may use one flourish (one per turn), spending a Bardic Inspiration use. Defensive Flourish: the die result is extra damage and is added to your AC until the start of your next turn. Slashing Flourish: the die result is extra damage to the target and to another creature of your choice within 5 feet of you. Mobile Flourish: the die result is extra damage, and you push the target 5 feet plus the die result away, then can use your reaction to move up to your walking speed to a space within 5 feet of it.

Extra Attack.title: Extra Attack
Extra Attack.desc_long: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Master's Flourish.title: Master's Flourish
Master's Flourish.desc_long: Whenever you use a Blade Flourish option, you can roll a d6 and use that instead of spending a Bardic Inspiration die.

Bonus Proficiencies.title: Bonus Proficiencies
Bonus Proficiencies.desc_long: You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and martial weapons.

Combat Inspiration.title: Combat Inspiration
Combat Inspiration.desc_long: A creature holding one of your Bardic Inspiration dice can add it to a weapon damage roll it just made. Alternatively, when an attack roll is made against it, it can use its reaction to roll the die and add the result to its AC against that attack, after seeing the roll but before the outcome is known.

Extra Attack.title: Extra Attack
Extra Attack.desc_long: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

Battle Magic.title: Battle Magic
Battle Magic.desc_long: When you use your action to cast a bard spell, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

Psychic Blades.title: Psychic Blades
Psychic Blades.desc_long: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can spend one use of Bardic Inspiration to deal an extra 2d6 psychic damage. Once per round, on your turn only. The damage becomes 3d6 at 5th level, 5d6 at 10th level, and 8d6 at 15th level.

Words of Terror.title: Words of Terror
Words of Terror.desc_long: After speaking alone with a humanoid for at least 1 minute, the target must succeed on a Wisdom save against your spell save DC or be frightened of you or another creature you choose. The fear lasts 1 hour, until the target is attacked or damaged, or until it sees its allies attacked or damaged. A target that succeeds has no idea you tried.

Mantle of Whispers.title: Mantle of Whispers
Mantle of Whispers.desc_long: When a humanoid dies within 30 feet of you, you can use your reaction to capture its shadow, which you keep until you use it or finish a long rest. As an action, you can spend the shadow to take on the dead person's appearance for 1 hour (or until you end it as a bonus action). You gain access to information it would freely share with a casual acquaintance, but not secrets. A creature can see through the disguise with a Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your Charisma (Deception) check, and you get +5 to yours. You can't capture another shadow until you finish a short or long rest.

Shadow Lore.title: Shadow Lore
Shadow Lore.desc_long: You whisper a phrase only one chosen creature within 30 feet can hear. It makes a Wisdom save against your spell save DC, and automatically succeeds if it can't hear you or shares no language with you. On a failure it is charmed for 8 hours or until you or your allies attack or damage it, believing you know its most mortifying secret. It obeys your commands and gives you favors and gifts, but won't risk its life for you or fight for you unless it already wanted to. Afterward it doesn't understand why it feared you.

Arcane Initiate.title: Arcane Initiate
Arcane Initiate.desc_long: You gain proficiency in Arcana and learn two wizard cantrips of your choice, which count as cleric cantrips for you.

Channel Divinity: Arcane Abjuration.title: Channel Divinity: Arcane Abjuration
Channel Divinity: Arcane Abjuration.desc_long: Present your holy symbol. One celestial, elemental, fey, or fiend of your choice within 30 feet that can see or hear you must make a Wisdom save. On a failure it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage (it must move away from you, can't end its move within 30 feet, can't take reactions, and can only Dash or try to escape what holds it, or Dodge if it has nowhere to go). From 5th level, a creature that fails and isn't on its home plane is also banished for 1 minute (as Banishment, no concentration) if its CR is at or below the threshold: CR 1/2 at 5th, CR 1 at 8th, CR 2 at 11th, CR 3 at 14th, CR 4 at 17th.

Spell Breaker.title: Spell Breaker
Spell Breaker.desc_long: When you restore hit points to an ally with a spell of 1st level or higher, you can also end one spell of your choice on that creature, provided its level is no higher than the slot you used for the healing spell.

Potent Spellcasting.title: Potent Spellcasting
Potent Spellcasting.desc_long: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

Arcane Mastery.title: Arcane Mastery
Arcane Mastery.desc_long: Choose four wizard spells, one each of 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th level. They are added to your domain spells: always prepared and counted as cleric spells.

Bonus Proficiency.title: Bonus Proficiency
Bonus Proficiency.desc_long: You gain proficiency with martial weapons.

Reaper.title: Reaper
Reaper.desc_long: You learn one necromancy cantrip from any spell list. When you cast a necromancy cantrip that normally targets one creature, it can instead target two creatures within range and within 5 feet of each other.

Channel Divinity: Touch of Death.title: Channel Divinity: Touch of Death
Channel Divinity: Touch of Death.desc_long: When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can use Channel Divinity to deal extra necrotic damage equal to 5 + twice your cleric level.

Inescapable Destruction.title: Inescapable Destruction
Inescapable Destruction.desc_long: Necrotic damage from your cleric spells and Channel Divinity options ignores resistance to necrotic damage.

Divine Strike.title: Divine Strike
Divine Strike.desc_long: Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 necrotic damage. This becomes 2d8 at 14th level.

Improved Reaper.title: Improved Reaper
Improved Reaper.desc_long: When you cast a necromancy spell of 1st through 5th level that targets one creature, it can instead target two creatures within range and within 5 feet of each other. If the spell consumes its material components, you must provide them for each target.

Bonus Proficiencies.title: Bonus Proficiencies
Bonus Proficiencies.desc_long: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.

Blessing of the Forge.title: Blessing of the Forge
Blessing of the Forge.duration: Until end of next long rest
Blessing of the Forge.desc_long: At the end of a long rest, touch one nonmagical suit of armor or simple or martial weapon. Until your next long rest ends (or you die), it becomes magical: +1 AC if armor, or +1 to attack and damage rolls if a weapon.

Channel Divinity: Artisan's Blessing.title: Channel Divinity: Artisan's Blessing
Channel Divinity: Artisan's Blessing.desc_long: Through an hour-long ritual you craft a nonmagical item that includes metal (a weapon, armor, ten pieces of ammunition, a set of tools, or another metal object) worth no more than 100 gp. You must lay out metal, coins included, equal to its value, which is consumed. It appears on a surface within 5 feet of you. You can duplicate a nonmagical metal item, such as a key, if you hold the original during the ritual.

Soul of the Forge.title: Soul of the Forge
Soul of the Forge.desc_long: You gain resistance to fire damage, and +1 AC while wearing heavy armor.

Divine Strike.title: Divine Strike
Divine Strike.desc_long: Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 fire damage. This becomes 2d8 at 14th level.

Saint of Forge and Fire.title: Saint of Forge and Fire
Saint of Forge and Fire.desc_long: You gain immunity to fire damage. While wearing heavy armor you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

Circle of Mortality.title: Circle of Mortality
Circle of Mortality.desc_long: When you roll dice to restore hit points with a spell to a creature at 0 HP, you use the highest possible result on each die instead. You also learn Spare the Dying, which doesn't count against your cantrips known; for you it has a range of 30 feet and can be cast as a bonus action.

Eyes of the Grave.title: Eyes of the Grave
Eyes of the Grave.duration: Until end of your next turn
Eyes of the Grave.desc_long: You detect the location of any undead within 60 feet that isn't behind total cover or protected from divination magic, until the end of your next turn. It reveals nothing about their capabilities or identity. You can do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once).

Channel Divinity: Path to the Grave.title: Channel Divinity: Path to the Grave
Channel Divinity: Path to the Grave.duration: Until end of your next turn
Channel Divinity: Path to the Grave.desc_long: Choose a creature you can see within 30 feet and curse it until the end of your next turn. The next time you or an ally hits it with an attack, it is vulnerable to all of that attack's damage, and the curse ends.

Sentinel at Death's Door.title: Sentinel at Death's Door
Sentinel at Death's Door.desc_long: When you or an ally you can see within 30 feet suffers a critical hit, you can turn it into a normal hit, canceling any critical-hit effects. You can do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once).

Potent Spellcasting.title: Potent Spellcasting
Potent Spellcasting.desc_long: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

Keeper of Souls.title: Keeper of Souls
Keeper of Souls.desc_long: When an enemy you can see dies within 30 feet of you, you or one ally of your choice within 30 feet regains hit points equal to the enemy's number of Hit Dice. You can't use this while incapacitated, and it can be used once until the start of your next turn.

Blessings of Knowledge.title: Blessings of Knowledge
Blessings of Knowledge.desc_long: You learn two languages of your choice and gain proficiency in two of Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for checks using those two skills.

Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages.title: Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages
Channel Divinity: Knowledge of the Ages.desc_long: Choose one skill or tool. For 10 minutes you have proficiency with it.

Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts.title: Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts
Channel Divinity: Read Thoughts.desc_long: Choose a creature you can see within 60 feet; it makes a Wisdom save. On a success you can't use this on it again until a long rest. On a failure you can read its surface thoughts while it is within 60 feet for 1 minute, and you can use your action to end this and cast Suggestion on it without a spell slot; it automatically fails the save.

Potent Spellcasting.title: Potent Spellcasting
Potent Spellcasting.desc_long: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

Visions of the Past.title: Visions of the Past
Visions of the Past.duration: Concentration, up to Wisdom score in minutes
Visions of the Past.desc_long:
Meditate for at least 1 minute to see shadowy visions of recent events, for up to a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom score (concentration).
Object Reading: holding an object, you learn how its previous owner acquired and lost it and the most recent significant event involving it; you can spend 1 more minute per earlier owner within a number of days equal to your Wisdom score.
Area Reading: you see recent events in the surrounding area (up to a 50-foot cube) going back a number of days equal to your Wisdom score, learning one significant event per minute, most recent first.

Bonus Proficiency.title: Bonus Proficiency
Bonus Proficiency.desc_long: You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

Disciple of Life.title: Disciple of Life
Disciple of Life.desc_long: When you restore hit points with a spell of 1st level or higher, the creature regains an additional 2 + the spell's level hit points.

Channel Divinity: Preserve Life.title: Channel Divinity: Preserve Life
Channel Divinity: Preserve Life.desc_long: Present your holy symbol and divide a pool of hit points equal to five times your cleric level among any creatures within 30 feet. This can't raise a creature above half its hit point maximum, and doesn't work on undead or constructs.

Blessed Healer.title: Blessed Healer
Blessed Healer.desc_long: When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain 2 + the spell's level hit points.

Divine Strike.title: Divine Strike
Divine Strike.desc_long: Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage. This becomes 2d8 at 14th level.

Supreme Healing.title: Supreme Healing
Supreme Healing.desc_long: When you would roll dice to restore hit points with a spell, you use the maximum possible number on each die instead (for example, 12 instead of 2d6).

Bonus Cantrip.title: Bonus Cantrip
Bonus Cantrip.desc_long: You learn the Light cantrip if you don't already know it. It doesn't count against your cantrips known.

Warding Flare.title: Warding Flare
Warding Flare.desc_long: When a creature within 30 feet that you can see attacks you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. Attackers that can't be blinded are immune. You can do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once).

Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn.title: Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn
Channel Divinity: Radiance of the Dawn.desc_long: Present your holy symbol to dispel magical darkness within 30 feet. Each hostile creature within 30 feet makes a Constitution save, taking 2d10 + your cleric level radiant damage on a failure or half on a success. Creatures with total cover from you are unaffected.

Improved Flare.title: Improved Flare
Improved Flare.desc_long: You can use Warding Flare when a creature you can see within 30 feet attacks a creature other than you.

Potent Spellcasting.title: Potent Spellcasting
Potent Spellcasting.desc_long: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

Corona of Light.title: Corona of Light
Corona of Light.desc_long: Activate an aura of sunlight for 1 minute or until you dismiss it with another action. You emit bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light for 30 feet beyond. Enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saves against spells that deal fire or radiant damage.

Acolyte of Nature.title: Acolyte of Nature
Acolyte of Nature.desc_long: You learn one druid cantrip, which counts as a cleric cantrip for you but not against your cantrips known. You also gain proficiency in Animal Handling, Nature, or Survival (your choice).

Bonus Proficiency.title: Bonus Proficiency
Bonus Proficiency.desc_long: You gain proficiency with heavy armor.

Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plan.title: Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plants
Channel Divinity: Charm Animals and Plan.desc_long: Each beast or plant creature within 30 feet that can see you makes a Wisdom save. On a failure it is charmed by you for 1 minute or until it takes damage, and is friendly to you and creatures you designate.

Dampen Elements.title: Dampen Elements
Dampen Elements.desc_long: When you or a creature within 30 feet takes acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to give it resistance to that instance of damage.

Divine Strike.title: Divine Strike
Divine Strike.desc_long: Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 cold, fire, or lightning damage (your choice). This becomes 2d8 at 14th level.

Master of Nature.title: Master of Nature
Master of Nature.desc_long: While creatures are charmed by Charm Animals and Plants, you can use a bonus action on your turn to verbally command what each of them does on its next turn.

Bonus Proficiencies.title: Bonus Proficiencies
Bonus Proficiencies.desc_long: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and in Intimidation or Persuasion (your choice).

Voice of Authority.title: Voice of Authority
Voice of Authority.desc_long: If you cast a spell using a slot of 1st level or higher that targets an ally, that ally can use its reaction right after the spell to make one weapon attack against a creature of your choice that you can see. If the spell targets several allies, you choose which one attacks.

Channel Divinity: Order's Demand.title: Channel Divinity: Order's Demand
Channel Divinity: Order's Demand.duration: Until end of your next turn
Channel Divinity: Order's Demand.desc_long: Each creature of your choice within 30 feet that can see or hear you must succeed on a Wisdom save or be charmed until the end of your next turn or until it takes damage. You can also make any that fail drop what they are holding.

Embodiment of the Law.title: Embodiment of the Law
Embodiment of the Law.desc_long: When you cast an enchantment spell with a slot of 1st level or higher that has a casting time of 1 action, you can change the casting time to 1 bonus action for that casting. You can do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once).

Divine Strike.title: Divine Strike
Divine Strike.desc_long: Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 psychic damage. This becomes 2d8 at 14th level.

Order's Wrath.title: Order's Wrath
Order's Wrath.duration: Until the start of your next turn
Order's Wrath.desc_long: If you deal Divine Strike damage to a creature on your turn, you can curse it until the start of your next turn. The next time an ally hits the cursed creature, it takes an extra 2d8 psychic damage and the curse ends. You can curse only one creature per turn.

Implement of Peace.title: Implement of Peace
Implement of Peace.desc_long: You gain proficiency in Insight, Performance, or Persuasion (your choice).

Emboldening Bond.title: Emboldening Bond
Emboldening Bond.desc_long: Choose a number of willing creatures within 30 feet (can include you) equal to your proficiency bonus. They are magically bonded for 10 minutes or until you use this again. While a bonded creature is within 30 feet of another, it can add a d4 to an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, once per turn each. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

Channel Divinity: Balm of Peace.title: Channel Divinity: Balm of Peace
Channel Divinity: Balm of Peace.desc_long: You move up to your speed without provoking opportunity attacks. Each creature you come within 5 feet of during this move can regain 2d6 + your Wisdom modifier hit points (minimum 1). A creature can receive this healing only once per use.

Protective Bond.title: Protective Bond
Protective Bond.desc_long: When a creature affected by Emboldening Bond is about to take damage, a second bonded creature within 30 feet of it can use its reaction to teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the first creature and take all the damage instead.

Potent Spellcasting.title: Potent Spellcasting
Potent Spellcasting.desc_long: You add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric cantrip.

Expansive Bond.title: Expansive Bond
Expansive Bond.desc_long: Emboldening Bond and Protective Bond now work when the creatures are within 60 feet of each other. A creature that uses Protective Bond to take someone else's damage has resistance to that damage.

Bonus Proficiencies.title: Bonus Proficiencies
Bonus Proficiencies.desc_long: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

Wrath of the Storm.title: Wrath of the Storm
Wrath of the Storm.desc_long: When a creature within 5 feet that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to force it to make a Dexterity save. It takes 2d8 lightning or thunder damage (your choice) on a failure, or half on a success. You can do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once).

Channel Divinity: Destructive Wrath.title: Channel Divinity: Destructive Wrath
Channel Divinity: Destructive Wrath.desc_long: When you roll lightning or thunder damage, you can use Channel Divinity to deal maximum damage instead of rolling.

Thunderous Strike.title: Thunderous Strike
Thunderous Strike.desc_long: When you deal lightning damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can also push it up to 10 feet away from you.

Divine Strike.title: Divine Strike
Divine Strike.desc_long: Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 thunder damage. This becomes 2d8 at 14th level.

Stormborn.title: Stormborn
Stormborn.desc_long: You have a flying speed equal to your current walking speed whenever you are not underground or indoors.

Blessing of the Trickster.title: Blessing of the Trickster
Blessing of the Trickster.desc_long: Touch a willing creature other than yourself to give it advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. It lasts 1 hour or until you use this feature again.

Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity.title: Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity
Channel Divinity: Invoke Duplicity.desc_long: You create an illusory duplicate of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet, lasting 1 minute or until you lose concentration. As a bonus action you can move it up to 30 feet, staying within 120 feet of you. You can cast spells as though you were in its space, using your own senses. When you and the illusion are both within 5 feet of a creature that can see the illusion, you have advantage on attack rolls against that creature.

Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows.title: Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows
Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows.duration: Until end of your next turn
Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows.desc_long: You become invisible until the end of your next turn, or until you attack or cast a spell.

Divine Strike.title: Divine Strike
Divine Strike.desc_long: Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 poison damage. This becomes 2d8 at 14th level.

Improved Duplicity.title: Improved Duplicity
Improved Duplicity.desc_long: Invoke Duplicity can create up to four duplicates instead of one. As a bonus action you can move any number of them up to 30 feet, to a maximum range of 120 feet.

Bonus Proficiencies.title: Bonus Proficiencies
Bonus Proficiencies.desc_long: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

Eyes of Night.title: Eyes of Night
Eyes of Night.desc_long: You have darkvision out to 300 feet (dim light counts as bright, darkness as dim). As an action you can share this darkvision for 1 hour with up to your Wisdom modifier (minimum one) willing creatures within 10 feet. You can share it again before a long rest by expending a spell slot of any level.

Vigilant Blessing.title: Vigilant Blessing
Vigilant Blessing.desc_long: Touch a creature (possibly yourself) to give it advantage on the next initiative roll it makes. The benefit ends after that roll or if you use this feature again.

Channel Divinity: Twilight Sanctuary.title: Channel Divinity: Twilight Sanctuary
Channel Divinity: Twilight Sanctuary.desc_long: A 30-foot-radius sphere of dim twilight centered on you moves with you for 1 minute (ends if you are incapacitated or die). Whenever a creature, including you, ends its turn in the sphere, you can grant it either temporary hit points equal to 1d6 + your cleric level, or end one effect on it that is causing it to be charmed or frightened.

Steps of Night.title: Steps of Night
Steps of Night.desc_long: While in dim light or darkness, you can use a bonus action to gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed for 1 minute. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

Divine Strike.title: Divine Strike
Divine Strike.desc_long: Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 radiant damage. This becomes 2d8 at 14th level.

Twilight Shroud.title: Twilight Shroud
Twilight Shroud.desc_long: You and your allies have half cover while in the sphere created by Twilight Sanctuary.

Bonus Proficiency.title: Bonus Proficiency
Bonus Proficiency.desc_long: You gain proficiency with martial weapons and heavy armor.

War Priest.title: War Priest
War Priest.desc_long: When you take the Attack action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action. You can do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once).

Channel Divinity: Guided Strike.title: Channel Divinity: Guided Strike
Channel Divinity: Guided Strike.desc_long: When you make an attack roll, you can use Channel Divinity to gain a +10 bonus to it. You decide after seeing the roll but before the DM says whether it hits.

Channel Divinity: War God's Blessing.title: Channel Divinity: War God's Blessing
Channel Divinity: War God's Blessing.desc_long: When a creature within 30 feet makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction and Channel Divinity to give it a +10 bonus to the roll, decided after seeing the roll but before the outcome is known.

Divine Strike.title: Divine Strike
Divine Strike.desc_long: Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra 1d8 damage of the same type the weapon deals. This becomes 2d8 at 14th level.

Avatar of Battle.title: Avatar of Battle
Avatar of Battle.desc_long: You gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.

Balm of the Summer Court.title: Balm of the Summer Court
Balm of the Summer Court.desc_long: You have a pool of fey energy: a number of d6s equal to your druid level. As a bonus action, choose an ally you can see within 120 feet and spend up to half your druid level in dice from the pool. Roll them; the target regains that many hit points and gains 1 temporary hit point per die spent. You regain all spent dice when you finish a long rest.

Hearth of Moonlight and Shadow.title: Hearth of Moonlight and Shadow
Hearth of Moonlight and Shadow.desc_long: At the start of a short or long rest, touch a point in space to create an invisible 30-foot-radius sphere of magic centered on it (blocked by total cover). Inside it, you and your allies get +5 to Dexterity (Stealth) and Wisdom (Perception) checks, and light from open flames isn't visible outside the sphere. It ends when the rest ends or when you leave it.

Hidden Paths.title: Hidden Paths
Hidden Paths.desc_long: As a bonus action, you teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Alternatively, you can use your action to teleport one willing creature you touch up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You can do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once).

Walker in Dreams.title: Walker in Dreams
Walker in Dreams.desc_long: When you finish a short rest, you can cast Dream (you as the messenger), Scrying, or Teleportation Circle without a spell slot or material components. This Teleportation Circle opens a portal to the last place you finished a long rest on your current plane (if none, the spell fails but isn't wasted). Once used, you can't do this again until you finish a long rest.

Bonus Cantrip.title: Bonus Cantrip
Bonus Cantrip.desc_long: You learn one additional druid cantrip of your choice. It doesn't count against your cantrips known.

Natural Recovery.title: Natural Recovery
Natural Recovery.desc_long: During a short rest, you choose expended spell slots to recover. Their combined level can be at most half your druid level (rounded up), and none can be 6th level or higher. You can't use this again until you finish a long rest.

Circle Spells.title: Circle Spells
Circle Spells.desc_long: Choose a land: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or Underdark. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain the circle spells for that land. They are always prepared, don't count against your prepared spells, and count as druid spells for you.

Land's Stride.title: Land's Stride
Land's Stride.desc_long: Moving through nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can pass through nonmagical plants without being slowed or damaged by them, and you have advantage on saves against plants magically created or manipulated to impede movement, such as Entangle.

Nature's Ward.title: Nature's Ward
Nature's Ward.desc_long: You can't be charmed or frightened by elementals or fey, and you are immune to poison and disease.

Nature's Sanctuary.title: Nature's Sanctuary
Nature's Sanctuary.desc_long: When a beast or plant creature attacks you, it must make a Wisdom save against your druid spell save DC. On a failure it must pick a different target or the attack automatically misses. On a success it is immune to this effect for 24 hours. The creature is aware of the effect before it attacks.

Combat Wild Shape.title: Combat Wild Shape
Combat Wild Shape.desc_long: You can use Wild Shape as a bonus action instead of an action. While transformed, you can use a bonus action to expend a spell slot and regain 1d8 hit points per level of the slot.

Circle Forms.title: Circle Forms
Circle Forms.desc_long: You can Wild Shape into a beast with CR as high as 1, ignoring the Max. CR column of the Beast Shapes table but keeping its other limitations. From 6th level, the maximum CR is your druid level divided by 3, rounded down.

Primal Strike.title: Primal Strike
Primal Strike.desc_long: Your attacks in beast form count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

Elemental Wild Shape.title: Elemental Wild Shape
Elemental Wild Shape.desc_long: You can expend two uses of Wild Shape at the same time to transform into an air elemental, earth elemental, fire elemental, or water elemental.

Thousand Forms.title: Thousand Forms
Thousand Forms.desc_long: You can cast Alter Self at will.

Speech of the Woods.title: Speech of the Woods
Speech of the Woods.desc_long: You learn to speak, read, and write Sylvan. Beasts can understand your speech and you can decipher their noises and motions. Most can't convey sophisticated ideas, but a friendly beast could relay what it recently saw or heard. This grants no special friendship with beasts.

Spirit Totem.title: Spirit Totem
Spirit Totem.desc_long: Summon an incorporeal spirit at a point you can see within 60 feet; it creates a 30-foot-radius aura and lasts 1 minute. You can move it up to 60 feet as a bonus action. Bear Spirit: creatures of your choice in the aura when it appears gain temporary hit points equal to 5 + your druid level, and you and allies in the aura have advantage on Strength checks and saves. Hawk Spirit: you can use your reaction to give advantage to an attack roll against a target in the aura, and you and allies in the aura have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks. Unicorn Spirit: you and allies have advantage on checks to detect creatures in the aura, and when you cast a healing spell with a slot, creatures of your choice in the aura also regain hit points equal to your druid level.
Spirit Totem.desc_short: Summon an incorporeal spirit at a point you can see within 60 feet; it creates a 30-foot-radius aura and lasts 1 minute. You can move it up to 60 feet as a bonus action.

Mighty Summoner.title: Mighty Summoner
Mighty Summoner.desc_long: Any beast or fey summoned or created by one of your spells gains 2 extra hit points per Hit Die, and its natural weapons count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

Guardian Spirit.title: Guardian Spirit
Guardian Spirit.desc_long: When a beast or fey that you summoned or created with a spell ends its turn in your Spirit Totem aura, it regains hit points equal to half your druid level.

Faithful Summons.title: Faithful Summons
Faithful Summons.desc_long: If you are reduced to 0 hit points or incapacitated against your will, you immediately gain the benefits of Conjure Animals as if cast with a 9th-level slot, summoning four beasts of CR 2 or lower of your choice within 20 feet. If you give no commands, they protect you and attack your foes. It lasts 1 hour with no concentration, or until you dismiss it.

Halo of Spores.title: Halo of Spores
Halo of Spores.desc_long: When a creature you can see moves within 10 feet of you or starts its turn there, you can use your reaction to deal 1d4 necrotic damage to it unless it succeeds on a Constitution save against your spell save DC. The damage becomes 1d6 at 6th level, 1d8 at 10th level, and 1d10 at 14th level.

Symbiotic Entity.title: Symbiotic Entity
Symbiotic Entity.desc_long: Expend a use of Wild Shape to awaken your spores instead of transforming. You gain 4 temporary hit points per druid level. While it is active, your Halo of Spores damage die is rolled twice, and your melee weapon attacks deal an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. It lasts 10 minutes, until you lose all those temporary hit points, or until you use Wild Shape again.

Fungal Infestation.title: Fungal Infestation
Fungal Infestation.desc_long: When a Small or Medium beast or humanoid dies within 10 feet of you, you can use your reaction to animate it with 1 hit point using the Zombie stat block. It stays animate for 1 hour, acts right after you, obeys your mental commands, and can only take the Attack action (one melee attack). You can do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once).

Spreading Spores.title: Spreading Spores
Spreading Spores.desc_long: While Symbiotic Entity is active, you can hurl spores up to 30 feet away to fill a 10-foot cube for 1 minute (ends early if you use this again, dismiss it as a bonus action, or Symbiotic Entity ends). A creature that enters the cube or starts its turn there takes your Halo of Spores damage unless it succeeds on a Constitution save against your spell save DC, once per turn. While the cube exists you can't use Halo of Spores.

Fungal Body.title: Fungal Body
Fungal Body.desc_long: You can't be blinded, deafened, frightened, or poisoned, and any critical hit against you counts as a normal hit unless you are incapacitated.

Star Map.title: Star Map
Star Map.desc_long: You make a Tiny star chart that serves as a spellcasting focus for druid spells. While holding it you know Guidance, have Guiding Bolt prepared (a druid spell that doesn't count against your prepared spells), and can cast Guiding Bolt without a slot a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus. If lost, you can recreate it with a 1-hour ceremony during a rest.

Starry Form.title: Starry Form
Starry Form.desc_long:
Expend a use of Wild Shape to take a starry form instead of a beast shape. You keep your statistics and shed bright light in 10 feet and dim light 10 feet beyond. It lasts 10 minutes, ending early if you dismiss it, are incapacitated, die, or use it again. Choose a constellation each time:
Archer: when you activate it and as a bonus action on later turns, make a ranged spell attack at a target within 60 feet for 1d8 + Wisdom modifier radiant damage
Chalice: when you cast a healing spell with a slot, you or another creature within 30 feet regains 1d8 + Wisdom modifier hit points. Dragon: you treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as 10 on Intelligence or Wisdom checks and Constitution saves to maintain concentration.
Starry Form.desc_short: Expend a use of Wild Shape to take a starry form instead of a beast shape. You keep your statistics and shed bright light in 10 feet and dim light 10 feet beyond. It lasts 10 minutes, ending early if you dismiss it, are incapacitated, die, or use it again.

Cosmic Omen.title: Cosmic Omen
Cosmic Omen.desc_long:
When you finish a long rest, roll a die. Until your next long rest you get a reaction based on the result.
Weal (even): when a creature you can see within 30 feet is about to make an attack roll, saving throw, or ability check, you roll a d6 and add it to the total.
Woe (odd): same trigger, but you roll a d6 and subtract it from the total. You can use this reaction a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

Twinkling Constellations.title: Twinkling Constellations
Twinkling Constellations.desc_long: The 1d8 of Archer and Chalice becomes 2d8, and while Dragon is active you have a flying speed of 20 feet and can hover. At the start of each of your turns in Starry Form, you can change which constellation is active.

Full of Stars.title: Full of Stars
Full of Stars.desc_long: While in Starry Form you are partially incorporeal, giving you resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

Summon Wildfire Spirit.title: Summon Wildfire Spirit
Summon Wildfire Spirit.desc_long: Expend a use of Wild Shape to summon your wildfire spirit in an unoccupied space within 30 feet. Each other creature within 10 feet of it when it appears must succeed on a Dexterity save against your spell save DC or take 2d6 fire damage. The spirit is friendly, acts right after you, and only Dodges unless you use a bonus action to command it. It lasts 1 hour, until reduced to 0 HP, until you summon it again, or until you die.

Enhanced Bond.title: Enhanced Bond
Enhanced Bond.desc_long: While your wildfire spirit is summoned, when you cast a spell that deals fire damage or restores hit points, roll a d8 and add it to one damage or healing roll of the spell. Also, a spell you cast with a range other than self can originate from you or from the spirit.

Cauterizing Flames.title: Cauterizing Flames
Cauterizing Flames.desc_long: When a Small or larger creature dies within 30 feet of you or your spirit, a harmless spectral flame appears in its space for 1 minute. When a creature you can see enters that space, you can use your reaction to extinguish the flame and either heal that creature or deal fire damage to it, equal to 2d10 + your Wisdom modifier. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus.

Blazing Revival.title: Blazing Revival
Blazing Revival.desc_long: If your spirit is within 120 feet of you when you are reduced to 0 hit points and fall unconscious, you can cause the spirit to drop to 0 hit points. You then regain half your hit points and immediately rise to your feet.

Arcane Archer Lore.title: Arcane Archer Lore
Arcane Archer Lore.desc_long: You gain proficiency in Arcana or Nature, and you learn either the Prestidigitation or Druidcraft cantrip.

Arcane Shot.title: Arcane Shot
Arcane Shot.desc_long: You learn two Arcane Shot options, plus another at 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level. Once per turn when you fire an arrow from a shortbow or longbow as part of the Attack action, you can apply one option to it. You decide when the arrow hits, unless the option involves no attack roll. Save DC = 8 + proficiency bonus + Intelligence modifier.

Magic Arrow.title: Magic Arrow
Magic Arrow.desc_long: Nonmagical arrows you fire from a shortbow or longbow count as magical for overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. The magic fades right after the arrow hits or misses.

Curving Shot.title: Curving Shot
Curving Shot.desc_long: When you miss with an attack roll using a magic arrow, you can use a bonus action to reroll the attack against a different target within 60 feet of the original target.

Ever-Ready Shot.title: Ever-Ready Shot
Ever-Ready Shot.desc_long: When you roll initiative and have no uses of Arcane Shot left, you regain one use.

Rallying Cry.title: Rallying Cry
Rallying Cry.desc_long: When you use Second Wind, choose up to three allies within 60 feet that can see or hear you. Each regains hit points equal to your fighter level.

Royal Envoy.title: Royal Envoy
Royal Envoy.desc_long: You gain proficiency in Persuasion, or, if you already have it, in one of Animal Handling, Insight, Intimidation, or Performance. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for Persuasion checks.

Inspiring Surge.title: Inspiring Surge
Inspiring Surge.desc_long: When you use Action Surge, choose an ally within 60 feet that can see or hear you. It can use its reaction to make one melee or ranged weapon attack. At 18th level you can choose two allies.

Bulwark.title: Bulwark
Bulwark.desc_long: When you use Indomitable to reroll an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma save and aren't incapacitated, you can choose one ally within 60 feet that failed its save against the same effect. If it can see or hear you, it can reroll the save and must use the new roll.

Combat Superiority.title: Combat Superiority
